newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia think tank sees economy slowing in 97. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Malaysia think tank sees economy slowing in 97. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]

text.p: Malaysia's economic growth is expected to slow further in 1997 after a sharp deceleration in the current year, a government-backed think tank was quoted as saying by the national news agency Bernama on Wednesday.
The Malaysian Institute of Economic Research (MIER) said it has revised its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth forecast for the current year to 8.4 percent from 8.5 two months earlier.
(Corrects GDP growth figures from "8.3 percent from 8.4").
The GDP growth in 1997 is expected to fall further to 8.2 percent, MIER said in its third quarter update of the "Malaysian Economic Outlook".
It said although strong demand pressures would continue, inflationary expansion would be fairly stable at 3.6 percent this year, edging upward to 3.7 percent in 1997.
Unemployment too would be stable at 2.8 percent in both 1996 and 1997, MIER was quoted as saying.
The report said the tight monetary and fiscal policies were expected to continue, which would slow down economic growth of Malaysia, now in its ninth year of over eight percent growth.
It said the economic growth would be supported by a strong domestic sector and the net external position would improve.
